correctness.rationale: Defant's greedy density proof applies to the prime tail beginning at \(5\). The source monotonicity reduces the tail inequalities to the stated finite check; the actual package checks \(F_4=1807104/2941225>39/64>6/\pi^2\). Hence the coprime-to-six tail closure is \([9/\pi^2,1]\). For a nontrivial \(2\)- or \(3\)-part, every local alternating factor lies between its exponent-one and exponent-two values, so its product lies between \(2/3\) and \(73/81\). The eight endpoint products in the proof chain from \(2/3\) to \(73/81\); their smallest adjacent ratio is exactly \(117/128\), and \(9/\pi^2<117/128\), so their scaled tail intervals cover the whole lower interval. Finally \(73/81<9/\pi^2\). Independent exact arithmetic reproduced all finite constants and the numerical gap.

final_claim: For Defant's alternating divisor function \(s_{-2}\), the range closure is exactly \[\overline{s_{-2}(\mathbb N)}=[6/\pi^2,73/81]\cup[9/\pi^2,1],\] and the two intervals are disjoint.
limitations: The theorem does not determine component counts on a neighborhood of \(2\) or for other nondense parameters.
